name: Ask the Book
headline: A conversation with your textbook.
summary: A hybrid RAG system that turns PDF questions into grounded answers with page citations.
role: Independent project · retrieval pipeline and application
status: Built · Streamlit may require sign-in or wake-up
problem: Textbook search should connect a question to the right passage, even when its wording differs from the text.
decision: Combine semantic retrieval with exact keyword matching, fuse their rankings, and rerank candidates before generating a cited answer.
result: The repository reports 9/10 correct answers on a small, custom phrase-matching evaluation. That is a development check, not a general accuracy guarantee.
lesson: Retrieval depth matters: increasing the context can recover a missing passage, at the cost of more material for the model to process.
next: Broaden the evaluation documents and questions before making stronger quality claims.

name: AlgoCoach
headline: Practice with a little more purpose.
summary: Codeforces submission analysis and explainable recommendations for the topics that need work.
role: Independent project · recommendation engine, API, and interface
status: Built · API cold starts can take a moment
problem: Choosing the next practice problem is difficult when a rating alone says little about which algorithmic concepts need attention.
decision: Weight topic relevance more heavily than rating in the feature vector, then use K-nearest neighbors to rank problems with an explanation of each match.
result: The application supports targeted Top-5 recommendations and a confidence-to-stretch Staircase. Async fetching and a disk cache reduce repeated upstream requests.
lesson: Useful recommendations need context: exposing matched tags and rating differences makes the ranking easier to understand.
next: Evaluate whether recommendations help users improve over time; a recommendation score alone cannot establish a learning outcome.

name: Arrakis
headline: Good tools deserve to be discovered.
summary: A team concept for discovering indie tools through short demos, trials, and useful feedback.
role: Team UNEMPLOYEDS · assigned frontend and scoring/leaderboard scope
status: Team concept · repository documents the intended architecture
problem: Student and indie projects can be hard to discover and try, especially for people who do not want to set up a development environment.
decision: The team proposed a discovery feed that connects a short demonstration to a trial and structured feedback. My assigned scope covers the Next.js frontend and scoring/leaderboard service.
result: The README records the product direction, team responsibilities, and target architecture. This case study describes that plan; it does not claim the complete platform has shipped.
lesson: A shared plan makes ownership visible, especially when discovery, sandboxing, recommendations, and scoring span different services.
next: Document implemented milestones and actual trial behavior before presenting the planned experience as a finished product.
